==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|id=noun|:inh|enm:use>|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|use}}, from {{der|en|fro|us}}, from {{der|en|la|ūsus|t=use, custom, skill, habit}}, from past participle stem of {{m|la|ūtor|t=use}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|note|t=use}} (see [[note#Etymology_2|note]]) from {{cog|ang|notu}}; {{cog|enm|nutte|t=use}} from {{cog|ang|nytt}}; as well as {{cog|ang|fricu}} and {{cog|ang|sidu}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{enPR|yo͞os|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/juːs/}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-use.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{enPR|yo͞os|a=GA,CA}}, {{IPA|en|/jus/|[jɪu̯s]}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-use-noun.ogg|a=US}} ** {{IPA|en|/(j)ɪu̯s/|a=Ottawa Valley}} * {{enPR|yo͞os|a=AU,NZ}}, {{IPA|en|/jʉːs/}} * {{IPA|en|/jʉs/|a=Scotland,Northern Ireland}} * {{rhymes|en|uːs|s=1}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # The act of using. #: {{syn|en|employment|usage|note|nait}} #: {{hypo|en|abuse|fair use|misuse|overuse|reuse|underuse}} #: {{ux|en|The '''use''' of torture has been condemned by the United Nations.}} #* {{quote-book|en|1962|w:Curtis Bok|Maria: a Tale of the Northeast Coast and of the North Atlantic||127|{{...}}long john underwear, heavy socks, rubber boots, thick flannel shirts, oilskins — it all wore and tore and sprung holes from the hard '''use''' of battling storm and bad weather.|location=w:[[New York City|New York]]}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} The act of [[consume|consuming]] [[alcohol]] or [[narcotic]]s. #* {{quote-book|en|2018|Timothy R. And, as their ubiquity spreads, so too does the debate around whether we should allow ourselves to become so reliant on them – and who, if anyone, is policing their use.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261018073655/https://www.theguardian.com/science/2013/jul/01/how-algorithms-rule-world-nsa|archivedate=18 October 2026}} # Occasion or need to employ; necessity. #: {{ux|en|I have no further '''use''' for these textbooks, but we may have '''use''' for all these other things later.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|rare}} [[interest|Interest]] for lent money; [[premium]] paid for the use of something; [[usury]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Much Ado About Nothing|2|1|text=DON PEDRO. Indeed, my lord, he lent it me awhile; and I gave him '''use''' for it, a double heart for a single one: [...]}} #* {{RQ:Taylor Holy Living|passage=Thou art more obliged to pay duty and tribute, '''use''' and principal, to him.}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} Continued or repeated practice; usage; habit. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=III|canto=I|stanza=13|passage=Let later age that noble '''vse''' enuie,}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|I|ii|passage=How weary, stale, flat and unprofitable, / Seem to me all the '''uses''' of this world!}} #* {{RQ:Sarpi History of Trent|para=96|page=43|text=For the {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== {{etymon|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:usen>|tree=1}} {{inh+|en|enm|usen}}, from {{der|en|fro|user|t=use, employ, practice}}, from {{der|en|la-med|uso|usare|t=use}}, frequentative form of past participle stem of {{der|en|la|uti|t=to use}}. Displaced native {{cog|enm|noten}}, {{m|enm|nutten||to use}} (from {{cog|ang|notian}}, {{m|ang|nēotan}}, {{m|ang|nyttian}}) and {{cog|enm|brouken}}, {{m|enm|bruken|t=to use, enjoy}} (from {{cog|ang|brūcan}}). ====Pronunciation==== * {{enPR|yo͞oz|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/juːz/}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-use2.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{enPR|yo͞oz|a=GenAm,CA}}, {{IPA|en|/juz/|[jɪu̯z]}} {{q|see usage notes}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-use.wav|a=GA}} * {{audio|en|en-us-use.ogg|a=US}} ** {{IPA|en|/(j)ɪu̯z/|a=Ottawa Valley}} * {{enPR|yo͞os|a=AU,NZ}}, {{IPA|en|/jʉːz/}} * {{IPA|en|/jʉz/|[jʉːz]|a=Scotland,Northern Ireland}} * {{hmp|en|ewes|qq2=in most accents|yews|yous|youse}} * {{rhymes|en|uːz|s=1}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # To utilize or employ. ## {{sid|en|utilize}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[employ]]; to [[apply]]; to [[utilize]]. ##: {{ux|en|'''Use''' this knife to slice the bread.}} ##: {{ux|en|We can '''use''' this mathematical formula to solve the problem.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/david-van-tassel David Van Tassel]; [http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/lee-dehaan Lee DeHaan] |title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/wild-plants-to-the-rescue Wild Plants to the Rescue] |volume=101|issue=3|magazine=w:American Scientist |passage=Plant breeding is always a numbers game. {{...}} The wild species we '''use''' are rich in genetic variation, and individual plants are highly heterozygous and do not breed true. In addition, we are looking for rare alleles, so the more plants we try, the better.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|often with ''up''}} To [[expend]]; to [[consume]] by employing. ##: {{ux|en|I '''used''' the money they allotted me.}} ##: {{ux|en|We should '''use''' up most of the fuel.}} ##: {{ux|en|She '''used''' all the time allotted to complete the test.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[exploit]]. ##: {{ux|en|You never cared about me; you just '''used''' me!}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=September-October|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/katie-l-burke Katie L. Burke] |magazine=w:American Scientist|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/5/in-the-news-47 In the News] |passage=Oxygen levels on Earth skyrocketed 2.4 billion years ago, when cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis: the ability to convert water and carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and waste oxygen '''using''' solar energy.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[consume]] (alcohol, drugs, etc), especially regularly. ##: {{ux|en|He '''uses''' cocaine.}} ##: {{ux|en|I have never '''used''' drugs.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[consume]] a previously specified [[substance]], especially a [[drug]] to which one is [[addicted]]. ##: {{ux|en|Richard began experimenting with cocaine last year; now he '''uses''' almost every day.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|with auxiliary "could"}} To [[benefit]] from; to be able to employ or [[stand]]. ##: {{ux|en|I could '''use''' a drink.}} ##: {{ux|en|My car could '''use''' a new coat of paint.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|with gender pronouns as object}} To [[suggest]] or [[request]] that other people employ a specific set of [[gender]] [[pronoun]]s when referring to the subject. ##: {{syn|en|go by}} ##: {{uxi|en|I '''use''' they/them pronouns.|I suggest or request that others use the pronouns they/them when referring to me.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2023|author=Brianna I. Wiens|author2=Michelle MacArthur|author3=Shana MacDonald|author4=Milena Radzikowska|title=Stories of Feminist Protest and Resistance: Digital Performative Assemblies|publisher=Rowman & Littlefield|isbn=9781666913521|page=92 |text=The "Older" [butch] group is maintained by three administrators who all '''use''' she/her pronouns and two moderators, one of whom '''uses''' they/them pronouns while the other '''uses''' she/her.}} # To [[accustom]]; to [[habituate]]. {{q|Now common only in participial form. Uses the same pronunciation as the noun; see usage notes.}} #: {{uxi|en|soldiers who are '''used''' to hardships and danger|q=still common}} #: {{uxi|en|to '''use''' the soldiers to hardships and danger|q=now rare}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=4|passage=Thou with thy compeers, / '''Used''' to the yoke, draw’st his triumphant wheels.|year=1873}} ## {{lb|en|reflexive|obsolete|with "to"}} To accustom oneself. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1714|author=w:Bernard Mandeville|title=w:The Fable of the Bees|location=London|publisher=T. Ostell|year_published=1806|section=Sixth Dialogue, p. 466|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/100127945 |passage=It is not without some difficulty, that a man born in society can form an idea of such savages, and their condition; and unless he has '''used''' himself to abstract thinking, he can hardly represent to himself such a state of simplicity, in which man can have so few desires, and no appetites roving beyond the immediate call of untaught nature {{...}}}} ##* '''1742''', {{w|Samuel Richardson}}, ''[[w:Pamela (novel)|Pamela]]'', London: S. Richardson, 4th edition, Volume 3, Letter 12, p. 53,[http://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/100024502] ##*: So that reading constantly, and thus '''using''' yourself to write, and enjoying besides the Benefit of a good Memory, every thing you heard or read, became your own {{...}} ##*: {{...}} we must be constant and faithful to our Words and Promises, and '''use''' ourselves to be so even in smaller Matters {{...}} ##* {{RQ:Thackeray Vanity Fair|passage=We are not long in '''using''' ourselves to changes in life.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1876|author=w:George Eliot|title=w:Daniel Deronda|section=Book 3, Chapter 24|url=http://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/7469/pg7469-images.html |passage=The family troubles, she thought, were easier for every one than for her—even for poor dear mamma, because she had always '''used''' herself to not enjoying.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|archaic|or|literary|_|except in past tense}} To [[habitually]] [[do]]; to be wont to do. (Now chiefly in past-tense forms; see {{m|en|used to}}.) #: {{ux|en|I '''used''' to get things done.}} #* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=48|book=I|passage=''Peter Pol'', doctor in divinitie used to sit upon his mule, who as ''Monstrelet'' reporteth, was wont to ride up and downe the streets of ''Paris'', ever sitting sideling, as women '''use'''.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|1 Peter|4|9|text='''Use''' hospitality one to another without grudging.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1693|author=Sir Norman Knatchbull|title=Annotations upon some difficult texts in all the books of the New Testament|passage=For in the Rites of funeration they did '''use''' to anoint the dead body, with Aromatick Spices and Oyntments, before they buried them.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1764|author=w:Horace Walpole|title=The Castle of Otranto|section=II |passage=I do not '''use''' to let my wife be acquainted with the secret affairs of my state; they are not within a woman’s province.}} #* {{RQ:Eddison Worm|page=8|passage=Such smokes '''use''' ever to go before the fire.}} # {{lb|en|dated}} To behave toward; to act with regard to; to treat. #: {{co|en|to '''use''' an animal cruelly}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-3|II|6|text=See who it is: and, now the battle’s ended,
If friend or foe, let him be gently '''used'''.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Luke|6|28|text=Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully '''use''' you.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Samson Agonistes|text=If in my flower of youth and strength, when all men / Lov’d, honour’d, fear’d me, thou alone could hate me / Thy Husband, slight me, sell me, forgo me; / How wouldst thou '''use''' me now, blind, and thereby / Deceivable {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Addison Cato|page=6|scene=ii|text=''Cato'' has '''used''' me Ill: He has refused / His Daughter ''Marcia'' to my ardent Vows.}} #* {{RQ:Swift Gulliver|part=I|page=43|passage={{smallcaps|This}} is an exact Inventory of what we found about the Body of the ''Man-Mountain'', who '''uſed''' us with great Civility, and due Reſpect to your Majefty's Commiſſion. }} #* {{RQ:Fielding Tom Jones|8|3|text=“I hope,” said Jones, “you don’t intend to leave me in this condition.” “Indeed but I shall,” said the other. “Then,” said Jones, “you have '''used''' me rascally, and I will not pay you a farthing.”}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1884|author=Margaret Oliphant|title=Old Lady Mary |passage="Oh, how dare you, or any one, to speak of her so! She '''used''' me as if I had been her dearest child. She was more kind to me than a mother. There is no one in the world like her!" Mary cried.}} # {{lb|en|reflexive|obsolete}} To [[behave]], [[act]], [[comport]] oneself. #* '''1551''', {{w|Thomas More}}, ''[[w:Utopia (book)|Utopia]]'', London: B. Alsop & T. Fawcet, 1639, “Of Bond-men, Sicke persons, Wedlocke, and divers other matters,” page 231,[https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/010945148] #* c. '''1558''', [[w:George Cavendish (writer)|George Cavendish]], ''The Life and Death of {{w|Thomas Wolsey}}, cardinal'', edited by Grace H. M. Simpson, London: R. & T. Washbourne, 1901, page 57,[https://archive.org/details/lifedeathofthoma00caveuoft] =====Usage notes===== * When meaning "accustom, habituate" or "habitually do (or employ)", the verb ''use'' is pronounced {{IPAchar|/juːs/}} (like the noun ''use''); these senses and hence this pronunciation are now found chiefly in the past tense or as a past participle ({{IPAchar|/juːst/}}), or in the (past) negative form ''did not '''use''''' (as in ''I did not '''use''' to like her'' or ''the dragoons did not '''use''' [habituate, become habituated] to the Russian cold''). In all other senses, it is pronounced {{IPAchar|/juːz/}} (past tense/participle {{IPAchar|/juːzd/}}). * See also the usage notes at {{m|en|used to}} (and {{m|en|use to}}) for more, especially on the
